title: In Japan, sees himself reported killed in action
displayDate: About September 1965, in his first days at Camp Zama
description: In the Army hospital at Camp Zama, Japan, within his first few days there, Larry saw himself listed as killed in action in Stars and Stripes. He says he was told of it at Camp Zama and then saw it or went looking for it. He went straight to the hospital chaplain and told him he was still alive, and the chaplain wrote it down in a book. The report was wrong: he was alive to read it.
researchNotes: 2026-09-14: re-dated. The founding brief's "Around August 1965" (paraphrase, data/recollections/2026-brief-kia-report.json) sorted this before he left Vietnam. His own later accounts put it after he reached Japan: "In the first 3-4 days I saw the name in the KIA list and went straight to the chaplin in the hospital in Camp Zama" (giscus-stories-c18259364, 2026-09-02, transcribed); "Was told of it at Camp Zama and then saw it or went looking for it" (giscus-stories-c18118868, 2026-08-22); Camp Zama "may have been 9/3/1965" (2026-09-03-phone-camp-zama-date, paraphrase); the chaplain "wrote it down in a book" (2026-09-03-phone-the-chaplain). The brief stays as given. Chain and dates: research/events/medevac-chain-1965.md. The DD-214 (cited) documents that he ended his service as a patient in Japan; it does not document the report. SEARCH RESULTS, replacing the old next-steps (full scope in research/events/kia-misreport-stars-stripes.md, kia-list-dcas-reconciliation.md, kia-same-name-hypothesis.md): same-name confusion for a fatal listing is a hard negative (no Hunnewell or near-spelling in the complete DCAS roll, 2026-09); the Pacific Stars and Stripes Vietnam casualty lists for September–December 1965 were located and read, and none names him (sessions of 2026-09-03 to 2026-09-13, NewspaperArchive subscription ending 2026-09-17); no Pacific item in 1965–66 uses "erroneously" or "mistakenly" about a casualty (which rules out a labelled correction in those words, not an acknowledgment buried in a later story). Surviving hypothesis, weaker to test: a release naming him was issued but never ran in the Pacific edition. Not searched yet: the Camp Zama chaplain's records. Captain Guegler (his own spelling Geutler) was linked here by the brief; in his own telling he is the officer who flew him off the mountain, not a figure in the report. Ledger #1 and #10, issue #9.
